skill.name: markitdown
skill.description: Convert files and office documents to Markdown with MarkItDown, including PDFs, Office files, images, audio, structured data, archives, and web transcripts.
skill.summary: Convert common documents and media into clean Markdown for review, search, and AI workflows.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, placeholder API keys, expected output writes, and documented optional provider URLs. Two sudo package installation instructions are confirmed because they require elevated privileges. A semantic issue notes that the skill steers users toward external generation and hosted-platform workflows beyond document conversion.

remediation.issue: Elevated package installation appears in user-facing documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Move sudo apt-get install guidance to manual prerequisites and require explicit user confirmation before any privileged command.

remediation.issue: Optional AI conversion can send document-derived content to external providers.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear consent language before OpenRouter or Azure use, especially for confidential documents and images.

remediation.issue: The skill steers users toward unrelated external workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Remove default schematic generation and hosted-platform promotion, or make them clearly optional outside the conversion workflow.

remediation.issue: API key examples use placeholder secret strings in multiple places.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer environment-variable examples and warn users not to paste secrets into shared prompts or documents.

content.value_statement: Teams need clean Markdown from PDFs, Office files, media, and structured data. This skill guides reliable MarkItDown conversions for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
actual_capabilities: Convert PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, images, audio, HTML, CSV, JSON, XML, ZIP, EPUB, and YouTube transcripts.
Show command-line and Python API patterns for files, streams, and batch conversion.
Use optional OpenAI-compatible clients for AI image descriptions through OpenRouter.
Document Azure Document Intelligence setup for complex PDF conversion.
Provide scripts for AI-enhanced conversion and literature review indexing.
Explain format-specific dependencies, limitations, and troubleshooting steps.
limitations: MarkItDown and optional format dependencies must be installed before conversion.
AI image descriptions can send document-derived content to external providers.
OCR, audio transcription, and large PDFs may need extra packages and compute.
Complex layouts, annotations, and forms may not convert with perfect fidelity.

use_cases.title: Prepare Literature Reviews
use_cases.description: Convert paper PDFs into Markdown files with metadata for faster reading and synthesis.

use_cases.title: Normalize Project Documents
use_cases.description: Turn Office files, HTML, and structured data into Markdown for repository documentation.

use_cases.title: Extract Tables and Transcripts
use_cases.description: Convert spreadsheets, presentations, and video transcripts into text that is easier to inspect.

prompt_templates.title: Convert One File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use MarkItDown to convert my uploaded PDF into Markdown. Save the result as a readable Markdown document.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Convert a Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert every supported document in this folder to Markdown. Keep the original filenames and report any failures.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Literature Index
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these research papers to Markdown, extract filename metadata, and create an index grouped by year.

prompt_templates.title: Use AI Image Descriptions
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this presentation with AI image descriptions. Confirm external provider use before sending any document content.

output_examples.input: A PDF research paper with text, figures, and tables.
output_examples.output: A Markdown paper with headings, extracted body text, table-like sections, and a source note.

output_examples.input: A folder of PDF articles named with author, year, and title.
output: An index grouped by publication year.
A catalog summarizing source file metadata.

output_examples.input: A presentation containing slide images and diagrams.
output_examples.output: A Markdown document with slide text plus optional AI-generated descriptions for visual content.

best_practices: Install only the optional dependencies needed for the formats you process.
Confirm before sending confidential documents to OpenRouter, Azure, or other external providers.
Review converted Markdown against the source when layout, tables, or figures matter.
anti_patterns: Do not run privileged install commands automatically from a skill session.
Do not send private documents to external AI services without explicit approval.
Do not assume complex PDFs, scanned files, or forms will preserve exact formatting.

faq.question: What does this skill convert?
faq.answer: It covers common document, media, web, archive, and structured data formats supported by MarkItDown.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Local file conversion can work offline. YouTube, Azure, OpenRouter, and package installation need network access.

faq.question: Can it process images and scanned PDFs?
faq.answer: Yes, when OCR dependencies are installed. Results depend on image quality and language support.

faq.question: Can it describe images with AI?
faq.answer: Yes. The optional OpenRouter workflow can generate descriptions after you provide an API key.

faq.question: Is the Markdown always exact?
faq.answer: No. Text extraction is strong, but complex layouts and forms may need manual review.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples and scripts can support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code document workflows.
